Documentation · v0.2.0

From installer to verified firmware.

The desktop shell installs in one pass. Add the compiler and simulator when you are ready to run the real verification path, then bring your own model to draft firmware from a plain-language goal.

01 · Install

Install Embeder

Download the current Windows x64 setup from the official GitHub release and run it. Embeder installs for the current user and creates a starter workspace on first launch.

Release integrity

Verify the installer before running it if your browser marks the unsigned community build as unfamiliar.

SHA-256 6E1CBEF44BEF8DAC29F943E31A77E72E7AFFAEECBFF452EE9FC1067323858540
Open the latest release
02 · Toolchain

Add the verification toolchain

The editor and grounded datasheet views work immediately. The real build path expects the following developer tools:

Arm GNU ToolchainRequired for Buildarm-none-eabi-gcc ↗ RenodeRequired for Build & Simulate1.16.x ↗ Python 3Optional — model-backed generation3.12+ ↗

Validated baseline: Arm GNU 12.2.1+ and Renode 1.16.x. Newer versions should be treated as unverified until the real integration suite passes.

03 · First build

Run your first closed loop

Describe what you want, or build the bundled sample directly. Either way, the verdict comes from real tool output.

  1. 1

    Open the bundled stm32-blink-uart workspace.

  2. 2

    Describe a goal, or edit and save src/main.c.

  3. 3

    Choose Build for a real ELF, or Build & Simulate for the UART assertion.

  4. 4

    Inspect diagnostics, evidence, citations, and the verifiability boundary.

04 · Model providers

Bring your own model

Embeder auto-detects a supported provider from the environment. With no key, generation falls back to deterministic grounded synthesis — the loop always closes.

PowerShell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "..."
# or
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "..."
# or
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = "..."

Keys stay local to the process. Generated drafts remain proposals until the deterministic build and simulation stages pass.

05 · From source

Build from source

Contributors need Git, Rust with the MSVC target, Visual Studio C++ Build Tools, and Tauri CLI v2.

PowerShell
git clone https://github.com/pksark06-beep/Embeder.git
cd Embeder

rustup toolchain install stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
cargo install tauri-cli --version "^2" --locked
cargo test --workspace

cd desktop/src-tauri
cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc tauri build `
  --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

Prefer the browser workbench while developing: cargo run -p embeder-desktop serves the same UI at http://127.0.0.1:8787.

06 · Architecture

Architecture

The renderer never decides verification state. A shared Rust API owns workspace access and launches short-lived, path-jailed MCP workers over stdio JSON-RPC.

PresentationTauri workbenchHTML · CSS · JavaScript
↓ invoke
ApplicationShared Rust coreTasks · workspace · evidence · tiers
↓ stdio MCP
WorkerDatasheetCMSIS-SVD
WorkerFirmwareARM GCC
WorkerSimulationRenode
07 · Security

Security model

  • The app checks workspace file paths against the seeded firmware project.
  • Generated builds run in unique temporary directories.
  • MCP workers expose a fixed tool catalog and reject traversal.
  • Model output cannot mark itself verified.
  • Process isolation is application-level, not an operating-system sandbox.
  • Model keys are read from the environment or local .env; the selected provider receives the key and prompt.
